title: Urgent: TTFT & tokens/sec degradation from mixed-precision kernel selection affecting hosted/dedicated/private
creator: Priya Khatri
description: Summary: Starting 2026-03-12 03:20 UTC we observed a reproducible TTFT (time-to-first-token) and tokens/sec regression across multiple models (redwood-large-v2, openlm-7b-quant, community-8b-ptq) in Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Impact: API P50 TTFT increased 2-4x for some customers; sustained token throughput dropped 30-60% for high-concurrency workloads. Affected surfaces: streaming chat endpoints, embeddings pipelines with long prompts, and multiplexed sessions on Dedicated pools. Hypothesis: a recent kernel-selection heuristic that prefers mixed-precision (int8/ptq) kernels for latency under typical seq-len skew is causing cache-thrashing and increased kernel preemption when the request mix includes long-context fp16-incompatible traces. The scheduler then performs repeated kernel swaps and microbatch reshuffles which amplifies tail latency and reduces tokens/sec. This behaviour is amplified on Dedicated and Private because of GPU affinity packing and on Hosted due to mixed-tenant model fanout. Temporary Mitigation (today): 1) Rollback kernel-selector heuristic to conservative path on canary hosts (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7421). 2) Add a short-term traffic policy to pin affected models to fp16-compatible runtime variants for customers with active escalations. 3) Deploy a per-worker quant-fallback circuit-breaker to avoid repeated kernel swaps (feature flag: runtime.quant_fallback_circuit). Long-term work: 1) Implement per-tenant kernel affinity scoring that accounts for sequence-length distribution and historical kernel-switch cost. 2) Improve telemetry to correlate kernel-switch events with TTFT/tokens/sec regressions. 3) Add a kernel warmup handshake to reduce cold preemption. Rollout plan: Canary rollback on 5% of capacity in Hosted and one Dedicated pool at 2026-03-14 09:00 UTC. If metrics improve (TTFT p95 down by >=25% and tokens/sec restored >=20%), expand to 50% and then full. Private customers: provide patch bundle and upgrade notes; recommend manual restart window. Owner and contatos: Luca Meyer (assignee), Aisha Nadar (on-call infra), Ben Chu (SRE). Communication: draft customer message and priority support threads opened in Zendesk for escalations #ZD-4789, #ZD-4791. Links: internal incident doc (confluence://rwd/runtime/INC-2026-03-12-kernel-ttft), metrics: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ttft/ttft-kernel-selector, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7421
comments: 2026-03-12 03:45 UTC — ALERT: Observability alerts triggered for Hosted region us-west-2: TTFT p95 increased from 180ms to 1.1s. Notified on-call SRE (Aisha).

2026-03-12 04:10 UTC — Initial triage: regression correlates with deploy of runtime-1.20 canary that introduced kernel-selector heuristic 1.20-rc3. Rolling metrics show kernel-switch spikes aligned with regressed traces. Priority set to P0.

2026-03-12 08:20 UTC — Reproduced locally with stress harness using mixed short/long sequence workload against redwood-large-v2 quantized variant. Observed repeated nvrtc/kernel load events and microbatch reshuffle. Hypothesis formed.
2026-03-12 12:05 UTC — Engineering decision: implement conservative rollback toggle and circuit-breaker. Eng PR #7421 opened (link above).
2026-03-13 02:30 UTC — Canary rollback started for 5% Hosted capacity and Dedicated pool eu-central-1; initial telemetry shows TTFT p95 improvement ~28% and tokens/sec up 22% on canary hosts.
2026-03-13 09:00 UTC — Private customer ACME Corp escalated: observed degraded throughput during peak. Sent manual patch bundle and restart window instructions; support call scheduled.
2026-03-13 15:40 UTC — QA: run regression test matrix across fp16, int8, ptq variants and multiplexed workloads; added e2e test that simulates kernel-switch churn (test id: runtime-e2e-531).
2026-03-14 07:10 UTC — Rollout to 50% capacity started. Monitoring policy to auto-pause if tokens/sec drop >15% or TTFT p95 worsens on stable hosts. Postmortem draft initiated.
2026-03-14 11:55 UTC — Customer comms: Support template finalized and engineering-runbook attached. Reach-out list compiled (VIP customers first).
2026-03-14 12:20 UTC — Note from Ben Chu: add kernel warmup handshake to backlog and link to ENG-1002899 for instrumentation.
